A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeepEyesV2 and RealX-Bench study. The main text, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison; localized caption overlaps in v3 do not prevent recovering the results.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training-data ablations, preliminary RL experiments, and tool-use analyses, including Tables 1–6 and Figures 4 and 6–8.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments and adds proprietary-model comparisons, TIR-Bench evaluations, and further tool-use analyses in Appendix A.3–A.5.

M1.justification: The backbone, two-stage training, rewards, and reasoning/tool loop remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 introduces a limited test-time extension, DeepEyesV2 w/ Rotate, providing a callable rotation function alongside code execution. Whole-image search is clarified, but v1's appendix prompt already specified that interface.

E1.justification: v3 adds TIR-Bench evaluation and a Rotated OCR subset, extending coverage to explicit zero-shot task/tool scenarios, including image-orientation recovery and maze navigation. These introduce substantially different evaluation requirements; the original training sources and benchmark coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 7–8 add code-enabled GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Pro to the existing perception/OCR/chart and mathematical-reasoning comparisons. These models already appeared in v1's RealX-Bench and search comparisons, but their participation in these particular comparisons is new.

E3.justification: The added experiments specify common prompting for proprietary baselines, zero-shot comparison of four models/checkpoints on TIR-Bench, and a Rotated OCR control with versus without a callable rotation tool. Original training budgets, hyperparameters, and existing evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds training-stage tool-category analysis in Figure 10, zero-shot generalization and rotation-tool tests in Tables 9–10, and before/after-RL cases including a maze failure in Figure 11. Figure 7 also expands tool-use reporting. Original ablations and error analysis remain, while v1's Capybara case study is removed.

E5.justification: The mean and standard-deviation display for tool-call counts in Figure 8 is retained. The added results introduce no evaluation run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their values, while Tables 7–8 add proprietary-model scores. New TIR-Bench results are 16.0, 17.3, 18.7, and 20.8 for Qwen2.5-VL-7B, DeepEyes, DeepEyesV2-SFT, and DeepEyesV2-RL respectively; the rotation-tool comparison reports 33.5 versus 38.3. Figure 7 adds post-RL HRBench tool usage of 78.9%, and new figures report additional trends and cases.

T1.justification: The reward definition R = Racc + Rformat is unchanged. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about two-stage agentic training, curated data, RealX-Bench, and adaptive integration of code execution and search. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3–A.5 adds interpretations concerning comparability to GPT-4o, evolving tool preferences, and transfer to unseen tasks, code operations, and callable tools. It acknowledges imperfections in the maze example's code. The original mechanism discussion and error taxonomy are retained.

D1.justification: Figure 11 adds abbreviated implementation examples for image preprocessing, rotation, and maze reasoning, while Appendix A.3–A.5 documents prompting and tool access for the new experiments. Existing training hyperparameters, full prompt text, and project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the TIR-Bench citation and positions it as an evaluation of unseen task/tool generalization. The broader related-work discussion is retained; the rewritten DeepEyes reference still identifies the same named baseline rather than a newly introduced comparator.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section organization are retained. v3 adds three appendix subsections, renumbers subsequent appendix sections, clarifies image-search wording, and makes small textual corrections, including author-name capitalization.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 7–10 and Figures 10–11; Tables 7–8 redisplay existing results with proprietary-baseline rows. It revises Figures 1, 3, and 7, relocates Table 1, and removes the former Capybara figure while retaining the other cases under new numbers. Figure 7 duplicates InfoSeek, and Tables 9–10 have overlapping captions.

improvement.justification: The proprietary-model controls and zero-shot experiments make the empirical evidence more informative, and the revised image-search illustrations agree with the existing prompt. These are useful additions to an otherwise stable study. Unspecified TIR-Bench sample/subset sizes, absent uncertainty estimates, and new figure/table presentation defects limit the overall gain.
